newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha back below $210, spreads in contango.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha back below $210, spreads in contango.

text.p: Near-term naphtha prices fell back below the $210 level on Thursday, renewing a six-month low recorded on Monday, traders said.
Naphtha sentiment remained bearish with arbitrage cargoes from the West overshadowing the market, they said.
First-half June open-spec naphtha was indicated at $207.00/208.00 per tonne, compared with late Wednesday's $213.00/214.00. It was quoted at $208.00/209.50 on Monday.
Reflecting the views of ample prompt supplies, the half-month spread from first-half June turned into contango.
The value of first-half June contract was assessed about $1.00 lower than second-half June.
The spread between the two trading periods was quoted at $1.50 in backwardation earlier this month.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading remained depressed with Japanese demand taking a seasonal downtrend, traders said.

Major regional supplier Indonesia's Pertamina has several tankers floating offshore to store LSWR cargoes as regular storage facilities were mostly full amid thin demand for prompt cargoes, they said.
